meta.title: Murder on the Crimson Carriage
meta.tagline: A railway dinner mystery with a timetable, a poisoned toast, and one impossible alibi.
meta.setting: The Crimson Carriage, a luxury sleeper train crossing the Blue Mountains in 1934.
meta.victim: Sir Reginald Pike, railway magnate and owner of the Crimson Line.
meta.loop: Search train cars, question suspects, compare the timeline, review notebook, accuse.

howToPlay: Search each train car to collect clues.
Question suspects. New follow-up questions unlock when you find related clues.
Use the timeline map to spot the impossible alibi.
Make a structured accusation: killer, method, opportunity, and evidence.
Use hints if stuck, but your detective rating drops.

locations.name: Dining Car
locations.description: White linen, brass lamps, a half-finished champagne toast, and the victim slumped beside the dessert trolley.

locations.name: Galley
locations.description: A narrow kitchen carriage smelling of coffee, caramel, and coal smoke.

locations.name: Sleeping Car
locations.description: Private compartments, polished mahogany doors, and a corridor where every minute matters.

locations.name: Observation Platform
locations.description: Cold mountain air, cinders on the rail, and a service bell rope leading back toward the galley.

locations.name: Conductor's Office
locations.description: Timetables, key hooks, telegram slips, and the official movement log.

public.bio: Composed, silver-tongued, and obsessed with railway manners. She hosted the private toast before dessert.
public.alibi: Claims she was on the observation platform admiring the valley when Sir Reginald collapsed.
public.suspicious: She handled the sugar service shortly before the toast.

private.secret: Sir Reginald had proof she had been embezzling from a widows' railway trust.
private.motive: He planned to expose her after dinner, ruining her public life.
private.lie: She says she never returned from the observation platform, but the bell-rope smudge and sugar residue prove otherwise.
private.voice: Polished, icy, corrects manners even when cornered.

questions.label: Ask about the toast
questions.answer: Sir Reginald insisted everyone raise a glass. I merely reminded the table that sugar belongs in tea, not champagne.

questions.label: Ask about the observation platform
questions.answer: The night air steadies the nerves. I was outside while the gentlemen argued over timetables.

questions.label: Ask about the sugar tongs
questions.answer: Those tongs? Every table had a pair. How could one possibly remember who touched them?

questions.label: Confront with the bell-rope smudge
questions.answer: A lady may call for service. That is not a crime. Though I admit... I briefly stepped back inside.

public.bio: A decorated veteran travelling with a locked dispatch case.
public.alibi: Claims he was asleep in compartment three during dessert.
public.suspicious: A blue military thread was found near the sleeping-car corridor.

private.secret: He forged war-supply records with Sir Reginald years ago.
private.motive: Reginald used the forgery to blackmail him.
private.lie: He was awake and searching for a stolen telegram.
private.voice: Blunt, formal, ashamed beneath the bluster.

questions.label: Ask about Sir Reginald
questions.answer: Pike was no gentleman. But old debts are not the same as murder.

questions.label: Ask about the blue thread
questions.answer: My sleeve tore on the compartment latch before dinner. The conductor can confirm the time.

public.bio: The headline performer in the lounge car, travelling under a stage name.
public.alibi: Claims she was rehearsing alone when the victim died.
public.suspicious: A threatening note in her handwriting was found torn by the wind.

private.secret: She is Sir Reginald's unacknowledged daughter.
private.motive: He refused to recognize her and threatened to cancel her contract.
private.lie: She wrote the note, but never sent it.
private.voice: Bright, quick, defensive when treated like entertainment.

questions.label: Ask about the torn note
questions.answer: Yes, I wrote it. I wanted him frightened, not dead. The station clock proves I was in the lounge before the toast.

questions.label: Ask why the argument was personal
questions.answer: He was my father, though he'd rather derail a train than admit it.

public.bio: Knows every table setting, timetable, and passenger habit on the Crimson Line.
public.alibi: Claims he was serving coffee in the dining car.
public.suspicious: His ledger shows a missing tea caddy key.

private.secret: He has been selling first-class passenger gossip to newspapers.
private.motive: Sir Reginald discovered the leak and planned to dismiss him.
private.lie: He hid the caddy key because it exposed his gossip notes, not poison.

questions.label: Ask about the tea caddy key
questions.answer: I misplaced it after luncheon. Foolish, yes. Fatal, no. I never touched the sugar bowl after Mrs. Vale corrected the setting.

questions.label: Ask who handled the sugar service
questions.answer: Mrs. Vale moved it. She said Sir Reginald's place setting was 'provincial'. I remember because she made me redo the whole table.

public.bio: A nervous doctor hired by the company after a previous accident scandal.
public.alibi: Claims he was examining a seasick passenger in the sleeper car.
public.suspicious: Only he could name the poison quickly.

private.secret: He falsified a medical report after an earlier Crimson Line crash.
private.motive: Reginald threatened to sacrifice him to protect the company.
private.lie: He recognized the poison because he treated it before, not because he used it.

questions.label: Ask how he recognized the poison
questions.answer: Bitter-almond breath, rapid collapse, tremor. I saw the same symptoms in a lab assistant years ago.

questions.label: Ask about the old crash telegram
questions.answer: Pike kept all of us on chains. But I was with Mrs. Harrow in compartment two at the fatal minute.

suspects.name: Violet Harrow
suspects.role: Heiress to a rival rail fortune

public.bio: Young, impatient, and publicly humiliated by Sir Reginald's latest business betrayal.
public.alibi: Claims she fainted in her compartment before dessert.
public.suspicious: Her ticket stub was hidden inside the victim's valise.

private.secret: She planned to buy the Crimson Line after forcing Reginald into bankruptcy.
private.motive: He stole her takeover offer and exposed her finances.
private.lie: She met him before dinner, but left angry and alive.
private.voice: Sharp, glamorous, more strategic than she appears.

questions.label: Ask about the ticket in the valise
questions.answer: It was proof he double-crossed me. I slipped it into his bag as a threat: I knew what he'd done.

questions.label: Ask about fainting
questions.answer: I did not faint. I said I might. People hear whatever makes young women harmless.

clues.title: Bitter Toast Glass
clues.text: Sir Reginald's glass smells faintly of bitter almond. The poison was in something added at the table, not cooked in the galley.

clues.title: Dessert Menu
clues.text: Dessert was plum tart with unsweetened cream. Several guests asked for sugar at the table.

clues.title: Rearranged Seat Card
clues.text: Mrs. Vale corrected Sir Reginald's place setting and moved the sugar bowl within reach of his glass before the toast.

clues.title: Silver Sugar Tongs
clues.text: Powder is caught inside the hinge of one pair of sugar tongs. The poison could be delivered as sugar crystals dropped into a single glass.

clues.title: Chef's Galley Ledger
clues.text: The chef signed out almond essence for dessert, explaining why the dining car already smelled faintly sweet.

clues.title: Locked Tea Caddy
clues.text: A locked caddy is missing its key. Inside are gossip notes and newspaper clippings, not poison.

clues.title: Hidden Ticket Stub
clues.text: Violet Harrow hid a rival railway ticket in Pike's valise to threaten him over a takeover betrayal.

clues.title: Torn Blue Thread
clues.text: A blue thread by compartment three matches Captain Mallory's cuff, but the tear happened before dinner.

clues.title: Sugar Smudge on Bell Rope
clues.text: A sticky sugar smudge marks the service bell rope on the observation platform. Someone with sugar residue called the steward, then returned inside through the service door.

clues.title: Narrow Platform Footprint
clues.text: A narrow shoe print faces inward, not outward. The platform alibi involved returning to the carriage, not admiring the view.

clues.title: Wind-Torn Threat Note
clues.text: Lila wrote that Pike 'would not survive the night as a fatherless tyrant.' Angry, but not operational.

clues.title: Conductor's Movement Log
clues.text: At 9:17, Mrs. Vale was recorded stepping onto the platform. At 9:20, the service door opened from the platform side. Pike collapsed at 9:22.

clues.title: Blackmail Telegram
clues.text: Pike threatened almost everyone aboard: a forged war record, an old crash report, a hidden daughter, and a stolen takeover deal.

clues.title: Stopped Pocket Watch
clues.text: The victim's watch stopped at 9:22 when he struck the table. Captain Mallory's compartment call was logged at 9:21 by another steward.

timeline.event: Dessert is served. Mrs. Vale complains about the table setting and moves the sugar bowl.
Sir Reginald receives a telegram and announces private talks after dinner.
Mrs. Vale steps onto the observation platform and is seen by the conductor.
The platform service door opens from outside. A bell rope is pulled.
The toast is made. Pike collapses after drinking from the glass nearest the sugar bowl.

hints: Do not start with motive. Everyone had one. Start with who could affect only Pike's glass.
The sugar clues are stronger than the dramatic threat note.
The platform alibi is not an absence. It is a route.

solution.motive: Sir Reginald was about to expose Mrs. Vale's theft from a widows' railway trust.
solution.reveal: Mrs. Adelia Vale poisoned Sir Reginald by hiding bitter poison in the sugar tongs, then using etiquette as cover to move the sugar bowl beside his glass. Her observation-platform alibi was not an absence: it was a route. The movement log and sugar-smudged bell rope prove she returned through the service door moments before the toast.
